movie_characters.description: The fun-loving, mischievous, yet brave partner of Jai; known for his humor, drinking antics, and the legendary water tank suicide scene.
The calm, sharp-shooter with a dry sense of humor; Jai's loyalty and silent love story with Radha left a deep emotional impact.
The ruthless, fearsome dacoit leader whose lines like 'Kitne aadmi the?' became cultural phenomena; the ultimate Bollywood villain.
The brave ex-police officer with a tragic past, seeking justice with stoic intensity; unforgettable for the big reveal of his missing arms.
The spirited, talkative tonga (carriage) driver whose fearless energy and famous non-stop chatter made her an eternal favorite.
The quiet, grief-stricken widow who finds silent solace in Jai; her haunting expressions conveyed volumes without words.
Gabbar Singh's loyal henchman, famous despite minimal dialogues — especially for being pointed at in the iconic 'Samba, kitna inaam rakha hai sarkar?' scene.
One of Gabbar's men who meets a grim fate; immortalized by the chilling line 'Tera kya hoga Kaalia?'
The hilarious, over-the-top timber merchant with an unforgettable Bhopali accent; his scenes became cult classics.
The comical, Hitler-inspired jailor who runs the prison with ridiculous tyranny and comic timing.
The loyal and compassionate servant of Thakur, key to the unfolding of the backstory against Gabbar.
Basanti's traditional aunt whose hilarious conversation about Jai's rishta left audiences in splits.
The blind but wise elder of Ramgarh who symbolizes the spirit and suffering of the villagers.
The brave young son of Imam Saheb who tries to stand against Gabbar’s gang but meets a tragic fate.
